samples.summary: Canonical share-link doc still says the Yorkie auth webhook is shadow/allow-all by default, contradicting the premise this delta's whole design rests on ("enforcing by default")
samples.evidence: Every comment added here (`docs-view.tsx:360`, `yorkie-doc-store.ts:593`, `yorkie-store.ts:84`) justifies the gate with "the Yorkie auth webhook, enforcing by default, refuses …", matching `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:5` ("Enforcing is the default") and `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:29`. But `docs/design/sharing.md:208-219` still reads "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode", and lines 231-235 repeat it; `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:39-42` and `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:447` say the same. A reader of the canonical sharing doc would conclude these new gates are unnecessary and that client-side read-only is the only boundary — the exact inverse of the branch's model. Cost stays inside the codebase (documentation divergence), but it is the doc that later share-link features will be designed against.

samples.summary: The "no doc.update() on a read-only mount" rule is implemented as a hand-placed deny-list per call site across five surfaces rather than one chokepoint, the shape the repo's own read-only store doc argues fails open
samples.evidence: This delta adds a `readOnly` boolean plus two `if (this.readOnly) return` guards in `YorkieDocStore` (lines 606, 3200) and three more in `YorkieStore` (constructor seed, `updateSelection`, `ensureAxisOrder`), joining inline `if (readOnly) return` guards in `board-view.tsx:601`, `slides-view.tsx:1132` and `pdf-collab.tsx:126`. `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:6-19` explains at length why the repo rejects exactly this shape — a deny-list "nobody remembers to extend fails *open*" — and both Docs and Notes already express read-only as an allowlist proxy (`readOnlyDocStore`, `readOnlyNoteStore`). The lessons file's own diagnosis ("the guard goes on the listener you were thinking about", after Board gated its cursor publish but not its selection publish two hundred lines later) is evidence the shape has already failed once in this PR. No shared seam (e.g. a presence-suppressing doc/store wrapper applied once at each read-only mount) was introduced, so the next presence write added on any surface silently re-wedges a viewer's sync.
